findings.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:968 — Reschedule-via-handleNewBooking passes immediateDelete=true (hard/immediate SendGrid cancel) while the functionally-equivalent reschedule path in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:490 omits it (soft-cancel only); two callers performing the same "cancel previous booking's reminders" operation now have divergent cancellation guarantees with no shared contract/doc explaining when immediateDelete should be passed.

packages/prisma/schema.prisma:634 — model WorkflowReminder gains a new `cancelled` Boolean field used together with scheduledDate in a WHERE filter (scheduleEmailReminders.ts) but no @@index([cancelled, scheduledDate]) (or similar) was added, forcing a full table scan as WorkflowReminder grows.

packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:966 — forEach with an async callback does not await deleteScheduledEmailReminder/deleteScheduledSMSReminder, so promises are fired and the loop (and enclosing try) completes before they settle, leaving the surrounding try/catch unable to catch async failures inside those calls

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:198 — deleteScheduledEmailReminder now performs prisma.workflowReminder.delete/update by reminderId with no ownership/userId filter, relying entirely on callers to have pre-scoped the reminder to the correct user; defense-in-depth is weaker than the prior explicit `booking: { userId: ctx.user.id }` guard even though traced call sites in workflows.tsx currently supply pre-scoped ids

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:177 — deleteScheduledSMSReminder now performs prisma.workflowReminder.delete by reminderId with no ownership/userId filter, mirroring the same defense-in-depth regression as the email reminder manager

packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:507 — remindersFromStep is fetched via `workflowStepId: oldStep.id` with no `booking.userId` scoping, so editing/deleting a shared team workflow step now also deletes/cancels the underlying workflowReminder DB rows (via the unscoped delete/update in emailReminderManager/smsReminderManager) for bookings owned by other team members, not just the caller; this pre-existing lack of per-booking-owner scoping is unchanged in intent but now results in actual DB row deletion where before it only cancelled the provider-side send

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:229 — catch block logs `Error canceling reminder with error ${error}` via console.log, which can include SendGrid response bodies (potentially containing referenceId/batch_id and recipient email addresses) in server logs

packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:376 — deleteScheduledSMSReminder was changed to conditionally call twilio.cancelSMS only when referenceId is present, then unconditionally delete the DB row; there is no test covering the null-referenceId path (skip cancel, still delete) versus the referenceId-present path.

goldens.comment: Asynchronous functions deleteScheduledEmailReminder and deleteScheduledSMSReminder are called without await inside forEach loops. This occurs during booking rescheduling/cancellation, and workflow/workflow step deletion/updates. Consequently, scheduled workflow reminders may not be reliably cancelled, potentially leaving them active.

When immediateDelete is true, the deleteScheduledEmailReminder function cancels the SendGrid email but fails to delete the corresponding WorkflowReminder record from the database. This creates orphaned database entries and is inconsistent with the immediateDelete: false path, which marks the record as cancelled. The SendGrid DELETE API call is also omitted in this path.

The 'cancelled' field is nullable, which can lead to existing records having null values instead of a default of false. This can cause incorrect behavior in the application when checking the cancellation status of reminders.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/bookings/lib/handleNewBooking.ts:968 — Reschedule-via-handleNewBooking passes immediateDelete=true (hard/immediate SendGrid cancel) while the functionally-equivalent reschedule path in packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings.tsx:490 omits it (soft-cancel only); two callers performing the same "cancel previous booking's reminders" operation now have divergent cancellation guarantees with no shared contract/doc explaining when immediateDelete should be passed.

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows two reschedule-related code paths cancelling prior booking reminders with different semantics for email reminders: handleNewBooking.ts calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId, true) (immediate SendGrid cancel via API), while viewer/bookings.tsx calls deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminder.id, reminder.referenceId) (no third arg, which per emailReminderManager.ts now only marks the DB row as cancelled=true rather than cancelling immediately). This creates a real, diff-grounded inconsistency in cancellation guarantees/timing across seemingly similar operations, but the diff alone doesn’t prove which behavior is “correct,” so it’s not a verifiable defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:198 — deleteScheduledEmailReminder now performs prisma.workflowReminder.delete/update by reminderId with no ownership/userId filter, relying entirely on callers to have pre-scoped the reminder to the correct user; defense-in-depth is weaker than the prior explicit `booking: { userId: ctx.user.id }` guard even though traced call sites in workflows.tsx currently supply pre-scoped ids

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, ...)` now directly `prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminderId } })` (when `referenceId` is null) or `prisma.workflowReminder.update({ where: { id: reminderId }, data: { cancelled: true } })` with no user/ownership predicate. In `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx`, prior explicit guarded deletes like `ctx.prisma.workflowReminder.deleteMany({ where: { id: reminder.id, booking: { userId: ctx.user.id }}})` are removed and replaced with calls to this helper. While callers may currently fetch reminders in a user-scoped way, the helper itself no longer provides the previous defense-in-depth check, which is a concrete, diff-grounded weakening but not provably exploitable from the diff alone.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:177 — deleteScheduledSMSReminder now performs prisma.workflowReminder.delete by reminderId with no ownership/userId filter, mirroring the same defense-in-depth regression as the email reminder manager

adjudication.rationale: The diff shows `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` changed to always run `prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminderId } })` (packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts) with no additional scoping (e.g., by booking.userId/teamId). That matches the finding: the helper now deletes by raw ID only, similar to the updated email manager which also updates/deletes by `id` without an ownership filter. However, in the diff the call sites pass `reminder.id` values obtained from already-scoped queries (e.g., previous booking/workflow reminders), so an actual unauthorized deletion exploit is not directly verifiable from the diff alone; it’s a defense-in-depth concern rather than a demonstrated defect.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/workflows.tsx:507 — remindersFromStep is fetched via `workflowStepId: oldStep.id` with no `booking.userId` scoping, so editing/deleting a shared team workflow step now also deletes/cancels the underlying workflowReminder DB rows (via the unscoped delete/update in emailReminderManager/smsReminderManager) for bookings owned by other team members, not just the caller; this pre-existing lack of per-booking-owner scoping is unchanged in intent but now results in actual DB row deletion where before it only cancelled the provider-side send

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show a behavior change: `deleteScheduledSMSReminder(reminderId, referenceId)` now deletes the `WorkflowReminder` row via `prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminderId } })`, and `deleteScheduledEmailReminder(reminderId, ...)` may update `cancelled` or delete when `referenceId` is null. However, the finding’s core claim—`remindersFromStep` is fetched with only `workflowStepId: oldStep.id` and no `booking.userId` scoping, causing cross-team deletion—is not verifiable from the provided diff because the query that fetches `remindersFromStep` is not shown. Additionally, for the specific “deleted step” paths shown, email cancellation with `immediateDelete: true` returns after canceling the provider and does not delete/update the DB row, contradicting the finding’s blanket statement that the change now deletes DB rows where it previously only canceled provider sends.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/emailReminderManager.ts:229 — catch block logs `Error canceling reminder with error ${error}` via console.log, which can include SendGrid response bodies (potentially containing referenceId/batch_id and recipient email addresses) in server logs

adjudication.rationale: In `emailReminderManager.ts`, `deleteScheduledEmailReminder` wraps SendGrid `client.request(...)` calls in a `try/catch` and logs the caught `error` via `console.log(`Error canceling reminder with error ${error}`)`. The diff shows this code path can be hit when cancelling via the SendGrid API (e.g., the `immediateDelete` branch), so whatever the SendGrid client throws could end up in server logs. The finding’s specific claim that recipient email addresses are included in the response body isn’t directly verifiable from the diff, but the general concern about leaking potentially sensitive API error details into logs is diff-grounded.

adjudication_records.issue_text: packages/features/ee/workflows/lib/reminders/smsReminderManager.ts:376 — deleteScheduledSMSReminder was changed to conditionally call twilio.cancelSMS only when referenceId is present, then unconditionally delete the DB row; there is no test covering the null-referenceId path (skip cancel, still delete) versus the referenceId-present path.

adjudication.rationale: The diff does show `deleteScheduledSMSReminder` now only calls `twilio.cancelSMS(referenceId)` when `referenceId` is truthy and then unconditionally deletes the `workflowReminder` row via `prisma.workflowReminder.delete({ where: { id: reminderId } })`. However, the finding’s core claim—“there is no test covering the null-referenceId path vs referenceId-present path”—cannot be verified from this PR diff because no test files or test changes are shown. Therefore the asserted lack of test coverage is not grounded in the provided diff.
